title: DeepHIV-AoU: A Multi-modal Deep Learning Framework Leveraging the All of Us Research Program for HIV Precision Prevention
text:
This project leverages advanced multi-modal deep learning and the All of Us Research Program
dataset to develop a precision framework for HIV risk stratification. By integrating electronic health records,
genomics, behavioral surveys, and non-medical drivers of health, the tool identifies individuals at high risk for
HIV acquisition and those likely to discontinue preventive medications. This research directly supports national
efforts to end the HIV epidemic by providing clinicians with actionable data to improve the delivery and
persistence of life-saving prevention strategies.

title: Advancing Functionality and Delivery of Miniature CRISPR Systems through Directed Evolution
text:
The large size of commonly used CRISPR nucleases limits their delivery. Miniature CRISPR systems offer a
solution but face challenges in efficiency and specificity. Leveraging directed evolution, machine learning, and
advanced delivery vehicles, we aim to transform miniature CRISPR systems into versatile genome-editing tools.

title: Vascular niche restoration to prevent delayed effects of acute radiation exposure (DEARE) in the hematopoietic system
text:
Delayed effects of acute radiation exposure to the blood system can be severe, including failure
of blood production and transformation to leukemia. Blood stem cells depend on signals from
nearby blood vessels, the “vascular niche”, for survival and regeneration after injury. We will test
whether therapeutic restoration of the damaged vascular niche can prevent blood system failure
and development of leukemia over time following acute radiation injury.

title: Genetically-engineered Bacteria Overcome Therapy Resistance
text:
This proposal in response to PAR-22-085: Microbial-based Cancer Imaging and Therapy - Bugs as Drugs, is
relevant to public health since it focuses on metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), a cancer
considered particularly difficult to target and generally unresponsive to current therapies. We propose to
investigate the systemic administration of genetically-engineered Bifidobacterium delivering a novel human IL-
2 (SumIL2) to the TME in combination with radiotherapy and/or immunotherapy. Our approach takes
advantage of the natural features and genetic engineering of Bifidobacterium to reinvigorate the immune
suppressive TME via systemic injection, and thus could have broad applicability in other hard-to-treat cancers.

title: Analytical Biochemistry Shared Resource
text: Analytical Biochemistry Shared Resource Summary The goals of the Analytical Biochemistry Shared Resource (ABSR) are to provide access to state-of-the-art mass spectrometry, advanced data analysis, and validated biomarker quantitative assay services to members of the Masonic Cancer Center (MCC). These goals are met through 3 Specific Aims: 1) Through the Mass Spectrometry Laboratory services, provide expertise on trace analysis of biologically important compounds, including DNA adductomic, exposomic, metabolomic, and proteomic services; 2) Through the Bioinformatics and Advanced Data Analysis services, process and analyze large and complex mass spectrometry -omics data sets, including DNA adductomics, exposomics, metabolomics, and proteomics data, and support and train users in the use of advanced data analysis software tools; and 3) Through the Biomarker Quantitation service, offer sensitive and quantitative methods for determining numerous chemical exposures in human urine, blood, or DNA. The members of MCC rely on ABSR staff for maintenance of instrumentation, guidance on related projects, method development, chromatography, and troubleshooting analytical problems. The Resource teaches and trains new users, including graduate students and postdoctoral fellows, on chemical analyses and mass spectrometric methods. New users receive one-on-one training from the staff on hands-on operation of both instrumentation and software. After training, the new users are usually capable of semi-independent use of most instrumentation. Experienced, trained users have continuous access 7 days a week. The less- experienced users operate the instruments under staff supervision. Dr. Peter Villalta (Carcinogenesis and Chemoprevention Program [CC]) has been the director of ABSR since 2019, before which he coordinated the Mass Spectrometry Laboratory for 20 years. Other key staff include Dr. Sharon Murphy (CC), who coordinates the Biomarker Quantitation service; Dr. Scott Walmsley, who is the Bioinformatics Coordinator; Dr. Linda von Weimar, who supports the work of both the Mass Spectrometry Laboratory and the Biomarker Quantitation service; and Dr. Yangchuan Zhao, an analytic chemist in the Mass Spectrometry Laboratory. Users are billed by the hour for instrument usage, with CCSG funds subsidizing the rates for MCC members. ABSR was used by 48 investigators in fiscal year 2022, of whom 37 were members of MCC.

title: Bundled Outreach of Multiple Cancer Screenings for Under-screened Populations (BUNDLE)
text:
Primary care clinics can successfully increase low rates of cancer screening using outreach strategies, but
most studies focus on a single cancer rather than all recommended cancer screenings. Therefore, we will
adapt and test a multicomponent outreach intervention (text, mailings, patient navigation) of multiple cancer
screenings (breast, cervical, lung, colorectal) as the BUNDLE intervention. This study is a collaboration
between long-term research partners that will engage at least 18 unique primary care clinics in Oregon and
North Carolina and reach over 1600 patients to improve early detection, prevention, and treatment of multiple
cancers.

title: Mechanisms underlying chromosome specific telomere lengths in yeast
text:
Telomeres length equilibrium plays a key role in age-related degenerative disease and cancer.
We discovered that, contrary to current models, each telomere has a distinct length distribution.
We will test the mechanisms that establish these distinct length distributions.

title: Motion and distortion-robust quantitative MRI of early brain developments
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it develops innovative quantitative medical imaging
technology that enables fast, efficient, and safe in-vivo evaluation of neurovascular structures and
characterization of normal versus abnormal brain growth in fetuses and neonates with perinatal stroke. The
proposed research is relevant to the NIH mission as it pertains to developing fundamental technology and
knowledge that enables the development of early preventive interventions that lengthen life and reduce the
burdens of human disability.

title: Creation of the Framingham Heart Study Cardiovascular Biobank and Atlas
text:
Our understanding of the pathobiology of complex cardiovascular diseases has been hindered by animal
models that do not recapitulate the spectrum of phenotypes observed in patients, limitations in access to
human cardiovascular tissue, and an incomplete understanding of the clinical phenotypic spectrum. We
propose to create the Framingham Heart Study (FHS) Cardiovascular Biobank and Atlas, consisting of a
detailed postmortem cardiac and blood vessel tissue repository and cardiovascular tissue-level omics (single-
nucleus RNA sequencing) from consented FHS participants, linked to rich longitudinal phenotypes and
circulating omics data across the lifespan. This unique FHS resource will advance our understanding of the
relation of cardiovascular risk factors with cardiovascular structure and phenotype and enable us to identify
new biomarker signatures for CVD in an unprecedented and systematic manner.

title: Psycho-neuro-immune Mechanisms Linking Stigma and Discrimination to Carotid Plaque Formation in Persons living with HIV
text:
Modified Narrative: Public Health Relevance Section
This study is relevant to the health of individuals at risk for atherosclerotic cardiovascular
disease who are predisposed to psychosocial stressors related to their HIV-positive
status. A multidisciplinary research team will evaluate laboratory and ecological
momentary assessments of the psychoneuroimmunological response to psychosocial
stress to further our understanding of the biobehavioral risk factors for coronary plaque
burden in people living with HIV.

title: Scaling clinical wearable foundation models for the detection of in-hospital deterioration
text:
This research is highly relevant to public health by developing and disseminating advanced AI-driven software
tools aimed at the early prediction of clinical deterioration in hospitalized patients. By enabling more timely and
personalized interventions, this work has the potential to significantly improve patient outcomes, reduce the
incidence of preventable adverse events, and decrease healthcare costs associated with acute in-hospital
deterioration. Ultimately, these efforts will contribute to enhancing patient safety, lengthening life, and reducing
illness for a broad population of patients in non-critical care settings.

title: Novel Quality Measures for Primary Care Management of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder
text:
There is an urgent need to develop meaningful quality measures for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder
(ADHD) treatment by pediatric primary care providers, as a prerequisite for improving health outcomes for
children with this highly prevalent condition. This project will leverage recent advances in machine learning
methods and engage key stakeholders to develop robust quality measures for ADHD treatment, and to prepare
for quality improvement interventions. The completion of this project will strengthen collaborations between
stakeholders to continuously improve evidence-based practices in primary care settings and mitigate health
disparities for individuals with ADHD and other mental and behavioral health conditions.

title: Examining somatostatin receptor pathways following binge drinking: a focus on PFC-->PAG projections
text:
Somatostatin (SST) functions as a brake on cortical excitatory signaling; however, this effect is decreased
following binge-like alcohol consumption in mice. The goal of this proposal is to determine how alcohol alters
SST peptide signaling onto glutamate projections from the prefrontal cortex (PFC) to areas implicated in aversion
and reward signaling such as the periaqueductal grey (PAG). Through this training fellowship, I will examine
differences in SST function, and in vivo neuronal signaling following binge-like consumption of alcohol in mice,
as well as develop necessary skillsets for a successful future academic career.

title: Cannabis use, PrEP and HIV transmission risk
text: This project seeks to investigate relationships between multiple aspects of cannabis use in relation to HIV prevention behaviors (e.g., pre-exposure prophylaxis [PrEP] use, adherence, and discontinuation) and biological vulnerability to HIV infection among populations in the United States heavily impacted by HIV/AIDS.

title: Developing Switchable and Functional Fluorophores For Multi-Functional Super-Resolution Microscopy
text:
This project aims to develop a library of switchable and functional fluorescent probes for
multi-functional single-molecule super-resolution imaging of live cells. I will encode
distinct single-molecule spectral features of the switchable fluorophores and integrate
them with a spectroscopic single-molecule optical imaging platform in the three
research thrusts to collectively achieve multi-functional nanoscopic imaging capabilities.
This project will allow biomedical researchers, for the first time, to achieve simultaneous
interaction imaging of multiple molecules and functional imaging of their surrounding
nanoenvironment which fundamentally regulate distinct subcellular processes.

title: Molecular Insights into Membrane Pathways of Alzheimer's Disease
text:
Alzheimer’s disease's pathology in the brain includes the accumulation of β-amyloid plaques related to key
membrane protein pathways. This project aims to elucidate the regulatory mechanisms of these key factors
using structural, biophysical, and functional techniques. The insights gained from this study will advance the
understanding of AD pathology and pave the way for innovative treatments that target these key proteins.

title: Targeting WNT7A Signaling in Pulmonary Fibrosis
text:
Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a fatal form of interstitial lung disease and there is no effective therapeutics
for the disease currently. In this proposal, we will test the hypothesis that the dysregulated signaling pathways
in the pathogenically accumulating basal-like cells in IPF promote fibrogenesis by activation of the WNT signaling
in the fibrotic niche, leading to impairment of AT2 renewal and fibroblast activation. This study will further aid us
to understand the biology and pathology of basal cell-mediated fibrogenesis in IPF and help us to develop
therapeutic strategies for patients with IPF.

title: An end-to-end informatics framework to study Multiple Chronic Conditions (MCC)'s impact on Alzheimer's disease using harmonized electronic health records
text:
We will build an end-to-end system to convert electronic health records (EHR) to Fast Healthcare Interoperability
Resources (FHIR) with integrated machine learning models to explore multiple chronic diseases (MCC)’s impact
on Alzheimer's disease. Partnering with ACTIVE MIND, an interventional trial that examines the potential efficacy
of cognitive training (CT) in reducing dementia incidences, we will develop a demonstration project to promote
the use of interoperable health records in clinical research by identifying and stratifying patients with Mild
Cognitive Impairment (MCI) who are at risk for developing Alzheimer's disease.

title: Developing AI-measures of Pedestrian Environment Features for Physical Activity and Cancer Prevention in Rural Communities
text:
8. Project Narrative
This research is critical for understanding the link between rural pedestrian resources and modifiable cancer
risk factors such as physical activity. Existing research has ostensibly focused on large-scale walkability
features that are infeasible to improve in rural areas, but substantial barriers exist to measuring more
changeable micro-scale pedestrian environment features (e.g. sidewalks, lighting) across rural geographies.
This project will overcome feasibility issues in conducting in-person audits of micro-scale environmental
features in under-resourced and expansive rural communities by leveraging artificial intelligence and assessing
the understudied link between disparate micro-scale pedestrian environments and physical activity among
middle to older-aged adults across the United States.

title: Immune checkpoint Inhibitor-Induced Autoimmune Diabetes: Immunological Mechanisms and Biomarker Discovery in Provoked Beta Cell Autoimmunity
text:
Immune checkpoint inhibitor (CPI) induced diabetes (CPI-DM), a rare but highly morbid endocrine immune
related adverse event (irAE), offers a unique opportunity to study beta-cell autoimmune disease. Identifying
genetic risk and immune features of CPI-DM will advance possible prediction and intervention for prevention
and treatment of CPI-DM, thereby furthering cancer care. Furthermore, these findings will illuminate steps
required for autoimmune destruction of beta-cells occuring in type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM).
